title: Flat Bedrock+
description: Data pack that converts uneven vanilla bedrock into a perfectly flat surface.
body:
![Thumbnail](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/796319499ff9e53ffc0d7847aa557d4839010e2b.jpeg)

Flat Bedrock is a data pack that converts uneven vanilla bedrock into a perfectly flat surface at Y = -64, without a significant impact on performance.

The data pack comes in two separate versions, depending on when you want to use it:

- One version generates flat bedrock during world creation
- The other version works on existing worlds by scanning the area around the player and flattening bedrock

Additionally, the existing-world version includes an admin option that allows generating flat bedrock over a selected area.

Flat Bedrock Worldgen
- Used at world generation
- Automatically creates a world with flat bedrock
- No additional processing required

Flat Bedrock (Existing Worlds)
- Designed for already generated worlds
- Scans the area around the player
- Bedrock blocks not at Y = -64 are:
    removed
    replaced with another block
- Result: a clean, fully flat bedrock layer

🛠️ Admin Features
- Generate flat bedrock in a 5×5 chunk area
- Generate flat bedrock in a 16×16 chunk area
➡️ Ideal for fast large-scale adjustments

🚀 Performance
- Optimized for low performance impact
- Lightweight for both servers and single player

Key Features
- Flat bedrock at Y = -64
- Support for new and existing worlds
- Built-in admin tools
- Low system usage
- Simple setup (2 separate data packs)

Requirements:
- Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.5-26.1.2

Installation:

Singleplayer
- Open Minecraft
- Create a new world and click on "More", "Data Packs"
- Drag the data pack into the Minecraft window
- Click "Yes" on the confirmation screen
- Move the data pack to the right-hand side of the screen by clicking the triangle on its icon
- Click "Done" and continue creating your world, then click on "Create New World"

Multiplayer
- Download the data pack
- Open your server folder, then open the folder of the world
- Put the data pack into a folder named datapacks
- Restart your server, and you can use your new data pack.

Permissions:
- None

Commands:
/trigger flat_bedrock.options
